correctness.rationale: In the canonical Euclidean H_n root embedding, the endpoint oriented normal cone is half the probability q_n that |X_1| is the largest absolute adjacent Gaussian difference X_j=(G_j-G_{j+1})/sqrt2. Adding closing increment X_n gives exactly q_n=1/n+E_n by cyclic symmetry, with E_n=P(|X_n|>|X_1|>max_{j=2..n-1}|X_j|). The conditional rare tail a(t)=barPhi(t/sqrt3)+barPhi(sqrt3 t), asymptotically sqrt3/(2 pi^(1/3))p(t)^(1/3)(log(1/p(t)))^(-1/3), p(t)=2barPhi(t). Nonadjacent interior exceedances are independent and adjacent joint tails are smaller; dependency-graph Poisson limit produces e^-u at np(t)=u. Regression suppresses adjacent excluded increments under the joint end event; independent alternating increments give an integrable exponential bound. Changing variable u=np(t), dominated convergence yields sqrt3 Gamma(4/3)/(2 pi^(1/3)); replacing 1/n by 1/(n-1) is lower order. This is analytical, not a Monte Carlo extrapolation; scalar coefficient independently evaluated.
